Gold Factor Regression — returns space, rolling 60-month

Gold (LBMA PM) log returns regressed on changes in macro factors — 10Y breakeven, 10Y TIPS real yield, DXY, WTI, VIX, MOVE, S&P 500, US Aggregate bonds — estimated in-sample (Newey-West HAC) and in a rolling 5-year window, at four frequencies. Numbers are scripted; this page only renders them.

Is expected 10Y-option vol a useful gold signal?

Incremental ΔR² and HAC t-stat of adding each rate-vol signal to the 7-factor core (minus MOVE). move=ΔMOVE (1m implied), rv10=Δ realized 10y-yield vol, vrp=Δ vol-risk-premium (implied−realized).

Contemporaneous vs predictive — can you trade it?

Across all frequencies: R² of the contemporaneous model (same-period factor changes) vs the lagged (t−1) model's in-sample R² vs its genuine rolling OOS forecast R². Forecast uses only prior-period info, so it IS tradable. Negative ⇒ worse than predicting zero.

Predictive factors (lagged t−1) —

Do last period's factor changes forecast this period's gold return? Plus gold's own AR(1) momentum.

Residual diagnostics —

On the contemporaneous in-sample residuals. These motivate the HAC standard errors.

Methodology & honest caveats

  • Dependent: LBMA gold PM, log return. Regressors: price/index factors → log return; yield/vol factors → first difference (change in level units). Never mix levels and returns.
  • Sample reaches as far back as the SELECTED variables allow (the engine drops only rows where a chosen factor is missing): full 8-factor model 2003-01 — the hard wall is the two TIPS factors (10Y real yield + breakeven); TIPS with a 10Y constant maturity did not exist before 2003, and any earlier "real yield" would be a fabricated proxy. Deselect them and the sample auto-extends: {DXY, oil, VIX, S&P, bonds} → 1990 (VIX inception); drop VIX → 1986 (oil/bonds); {DXY, S&P} → 1971 (DXY).
  • Per-factor first dates: gold 1968, DXY 1971, oil (WTI) 1986, bonds 1986 (see splice), VIX 1990, MOVE 2002-11, 10Y real & breakeven 2003-01. The OOS-by-frequency table shows the live sample start for your current selection.
  • Bond factor splice (integrity-checked): AGG ETF from 2003-09; before that, VBMFX (Vanguard Total Bond — a genuine Bloomberg-US-Agg index fund, monthly-return corr 0.978 vs AGG) ratio-spliced at the seam to extend bonds to 1986-12. No fabricated data; one documented seam.
  • S&P factor is price return (^GSPC), not total return — index dividends (~2%/yr) are a small constant absorbed into α; labeled honestly.
  • Alignment: each series resampled to period-END last-valid obs, transformed on its own consecutive observations, reindexed to a per-frequency master grid. No level is forward-filled → no fabricated moves.
  • Inference: Newey-West HAC standard errors (autocorrelation + heteroskedasticity robust). Bandwidth = max(data-driven 4·(n/100)^(2/9), ~1 period at this frequency).
  • Read std β and uni r, not raw β alone — raw β are unit-dependent (a per-bp MOVE β looks tiny). AGG: its expected sign is positive univariately, but in the multivariate model real-10y absorbs the rate channel and AGG's partial β can flip (suppressor; VIF↑). Read uni r alongside.
  • Pseudo-OOS: betas fit on the trailing 5y window, applied to the same period's contemporaneous factor changes — a generalization test of the contemporaneous relationship, not a forecast (it needs today's factor moves, so it is not tradable).
  • The intercept is large and significant (~+11–13%/yr): these factors explain gold's volatility and comovement but not its 2003–2026 secular drift, which lives in α. A returns-factor model is a risk/hedging lens here, not a return attribution that closes.
  • Explanatory, not forecastable (Predictive tab): lagging the factors one period collapses R² to near zero and the genuine OOS forecast R² goes ≤0 at weekly/monthly/quarterly. A few lagged factors (e.g. S&P 500) are individually significant in-sample but that does not survive out-of-sample — gold prices the macro factors within the period. Gold's own AR(1) momentum is insignificant.
  • Diagnostics motivate HAC: Breusch–Pagan rejects homoskedasticity at daily/weekly, Ljung–Box finds residual autocorrelation at daily/monthly, Jarque–Bera rejects normality (fat tails), and the design condition number (~2,000–3,500) confirms the real-rate/AGG collinearity — all of which the Newey-West HAC SEs are robust to.
  • Quarterly rolling windows have thin DoF (20 obs, 8 regressors) — betas are noisy; weight the daily/weekly/monthly evidence.
